issue_context.title: Improve enum parsing in config binder generator
comments: Will keep this assigned to me; but happy to take a community contribution here.

review_comments: I'd avoid preprocessor directives here. The parser could check/register whether this method exists in the input compilation and then we can emit the right implementation.

I'm torn about this. While I don't like that the generated code includes pre-processor directives, at the same time this has the nice property of being consistent in what code is being generated regardless of TFM. This might be useful if you were using the source generator in a multi-targeted project: seeing the same generated source regardless of how you choose to navigate to it in the IDE.

For this particular change I would recommend polyfilling the `Enum.Parse<T>` method for netfx/ns2.0 targets.

I'd prefer @layomia's suggestion of checking whether `Enum.Parse<T>` is available, emitting the code to use it if it is, and otherwise falling back to something else.  That results in the best code being emitted for the target platform. We also can't currently polyfill static methods like this well, since we lack extension statics; polyfilling here would mean emitting a helper that's used on all platforms, and then changing the implementation of that helper based on what APIs are available, at which point you might as well just do so at the call site instead.

> That results in the best code being emitted for the target platform

I'm somewhat apprehensive about this. Adding this kind of branching makes emitter code harder to maintain so we should be deliberate about where and why we do this. If a particular new API is performance sensitive we could hide it behind an emitted helper, polyfill it, or put it in an API that the generated code is calling.

> Adding this kind of branching makes emitter code harder to maintain

Not really: you have a helper in the source generator that emits Enum.Parse, and that one function emits the right variation.  Here we're talking about the difference between emitting `(T)Enum.Parse(typeof(T), ` and `Enum.Parse<T>(`.

> polyfill it

How do you propose polyfilling `Enum.Parse`?

> hide it behind an emitted helper

That would mean always emitting an extra method, even when it's pointless, and that method then contains the call that could have just been at the call site.

We should prioritize emitting the cleanest / best code possible. `Enum.Parse<T>` is both simpler to read and more efficient.

> Here we're talking about the difference between emitting (T)Enum.Parse(typeof(T),  and Enum.Parse<T>.

I guess I was trying to make a remark about this problem in the general case. It seems a helper on the emitter that produces the relevant expression would work nicely here. 

I'm mostly concerned about the combinatorial complexity that can arise from a code fragment containing multiple sub-expressions that _could_ avail of new APIs/language features. We should be selective about where and why we do this, using the latest APIs isn't a goal in and of itself. A source generator such as the configuration binder or STJ should ideally just be producing trivial glue code for object graph traversal.
Is there any update on what direction (polyfill/check method existance) should I take for my follow up PR ?

I believe the consensus is to generate the best code for the target platform - https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89823#discussion_r1283352188. In general, we'd want to watch for any complexity that may arise with generating different code across TFMs but in this case it's fine.
We should never fall into this case based on other diffs above.

I think the parser should not include enum types in the `PrimitivesForHelperGen` list. The emitter should have minimal/no post-processing of the input data. The `SourceGenerationSpec` could have a boolean property indicating whether an enum was part of the input graph.
